Long boring story but if you're interested: I started gaming because I bought my husband a PS3, and a particular game for it (Far Cry 3, if anyone cares), and every night after dinner he would play it. I'd bought it to keep him busy while I worked but the scenery was so gorgeous and the gameplay and story were so fun and engaging that I started watching him instead.

We started playing it "together" every night: I'd look up a walkthrough online (which is people telling you where to go/what to do/how to solve the puzzle or tips for getting past that part or whatever) to talk him through difficult stuff. Far Cry 3 turned out to be (IMO) one of the greatest games ever made (it's still my favorite game of all time, and I have played it through myself like five times), and honestly, we just started having fun doing that--me watching, him playing. It was a way we could do it together--it wasn't just him playing while I did my own thing, it was us deciding together where he would go, what he would do, when to start the next story mission, etc. And the game has such a gorgeous setting, that we actually just enjoyed having him run around and blow things up in this tropical paradise or singing long to the music on the radio as he drove a car around (there's only like a dozen songs that play on the in-game radio, lol); it felt like taking a little vacation every time he fired it up.

Eventually I decided to try playing it myself--it was easier after having watched him do it so much--and that was kind of it. I got really into a few other games, too--I am a huge Assassin's Creed girl (and those are the games with the really involved lore, where I've looked stuff up in videos to get caught up), but we still often pick games to play "together," where he'll play and I'll watch or we switch back and forth. The Batman Arkham games have these challenge sections, where you just fight bad guys trying to get high scores (or sometimes you have to sneak around a room silently taking them out), and a lot of the time we'll pick a challenge and compete with each other for the highest score.

TL;DR It can actually be fun to watch someone playing a game, if you're there in the room with them (and it's the right type of game; not all of them are fun for spectators). And it gave my husband and I something fun to do together that didn't cost a lot of money. But it's fun for my husband and I because, well, we have fun together. It's not the same fun to watch a stranger you don't know; it's fun for us because we're there in the same room, talking as we go, making decisions and competing and such. So I don't get the appeal of watching YouTubers play a game so much, because to me the fun comes from doing it with my husband, together (or from playing on my own). I've actually recommended it to other couples looking for things to do together, because we really do have such a good time.
